summary: This PR adds an average_age helper, a user search, pagination, and avatar loading. It has serious security problems. The search query is built by string concatenation, which allows SQL injection. load_avatar can read any file on the server (path traversal). An API key is hardcoded in the source. There are also bugs: an off-by-one in pagination, division by zero on an empty list, and leaked database connections and file handles.

findings.title: SQL injection in search_users via string concatenation.
findings.explanation: User-controlled `name` is put straight into the SQL string. Input like `' OR 1=1 --` or a UNION payload can dump or change any table.
findings.suggestion: Use a parameterized query: `db.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE name LIKE ?", (f"%{name}%",))`.

findings.title: Path traversal in load_avatar.
findings.explanation: A `filename` like `../../etc/passwd` or an absolute path lets a caller read any file the process can access.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the path and check that it stays inside the avatars directory: `base = Path('avatars').resolve(); p = (base / filename).resolve(); if not p.is_relative_to(base): raise ValueError`. Better still, allow only safe basenames.

findings.title: API key hardcoded in source.
findings.explanation: Secrets committed to the repo end up in version history and are visible to anyone with access to the code.
findings.suggestion: Load the key from an environment variable or a secrets manager (`os.environ["API_KEY"]`) and rotate the exposed key.

findings.title: Off-by-one in get_page: page 1 skips the first page.
findings.explanation: The docstring says pages start at 1, but `start = page * per_page` makes page 1 return items 10-19, so the first page can never be returned.

findings.title: ZeroDivisionError when users is empty.
findings.explanation: `len(users)` is 0 for an empty list, so the function raises an unhandled exception.
findings.suggestion: Return None or 0 for an empty list, or raise a clear ValueError: `if not users: return None`.

findings.title: Database connection never closed in search_users.
findings.explanation: Each call opens a sqlite connection and never closes it, so connections and file handles leak under load.
findings.suggestion: Use `with closing(get_db()) as db:` or call db.close() in a try/finally block, as get_user does.

findings.title: File handle leaked in load_avatar.
findings.explanation: The file is opened without being closed, so the handle stays open until garbage collection.

suggested_tests.description: search_users with input `' OR '1'='1` returns no rows (or only literal matches) and does not raise, which confirms the query is parameterized.
get_page(list(range(25)), 1) returns [0..9], page 3 returns [20..24], and page 0 raises ValueError.
load_avatar('../users.py') and load_avatar('/etc/passwd') raise an error instead of returning file contents.
average_age([]) is handled gracefully (returns None or raises ValueError), and average_age([{'age':20},{'age':30}]) == 25.
